windows.title: A number method that travelled
windows.studentText: The digits we use belong to the Hindu-Arabic numeral tradition. Place-value methods developed in India. Scholars working in the Islamic world studied, explained and transmitted them. Around the ninth century, al-Khwarizmi wrote about calculating with Hindu numerals. Knowledge travelled because people made methods clear enough for others to use.
windows.inquiry: Why does a place-value system make a large civic record easier to store, check and calculate with?
windows.modernConnection: Modern spreadsheets and databases still depend on each digit keeping a precise position.
windows.teacherNote: Say developed, described and transmitted—not invented by one person. Al-Khwarizmi's original Arabic arithmetic text is lost; later Latin versions survive in changed form.
